parole.significato: won (currency)
parole.testo: Borrowed from Korean 원 (won).

parole.significato: dan
parole.testo: From Korean 단 (dan) and/or Japanese 段 (dan).

parole.significato: gat (a traditional Korean hat made of horsehair, once worn by married gentlemen)
parole.testo: Borrowed from Korean 갓 (gat).

parole.significato: kimchi
parole.testo: Borrowed from Korean 김치 (gimchi).

parole.significato: kimchi
parole.testo: Borrowed from Korean 김치 (gimchi).

parole.significato: Hallyu, the Korean Wave
parole.testo: Calque of Korean 한류(韓流) (Hallyu, “Korean current”), from корейская (korejskaja, “Korean”) + волна (volna, “wave”).

parole.significato: an ethnic Korean in Russia and other post-Soviet states; Koryo-saram (used as an autonym)
parole.testo: Borrowed from Korean 고려 사람 (goryeo saram), from 고려(高麗) (Goryeo) + 사람 (saram, “person”).

parole.significato: makgeolli (makkoli), a traditional alcoholic beverage in Korea, made of rice.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Korean 막걸리 (makgeolli).

parole.significato: maknae (youngest member of an idol group)
parole.testo: Borrowed from Korean 막내 (mangnae), with the spelling likely influenced by English maknae.

parole.significato: mandu (a dumpling in Korean cuisine)
parole.testo: Borrowed from Korean 만두 (mandu).

parole.significato: manhwa (Korean comic)
parole.testo: Borrowed from Korean 만화(漫畫) (manhwa), from Japanese 漫(まん)画(が) (manga). Doublet of ма́нга (mánga) and маньхуа́ (manʹxuá).

parole.significato: unnie (elder sister, or an affectionate term of address for a somewhat older woman)
parole.testo: Borrowed from Korean 언니 (eonni, “older sister of a woman”).

parole.significato: pukjai (a kind of soup, similar to the South Korean doenjangjjigae, but usually eaten among Soviet Koreans)
parole.testo: Borrowed from Korean 북자이 (bukjai) (in today's South Korea, 북장). Essentially from the Soviet Korean dialect (a variety of the Hamgyeong-do dialect).

parole.significato: bulgogi, a Korean dish of shredded beef with vegetables.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Korean 불고기 (bulgogi).

parole.significato: soju, a Korean distilled alcoholic beverage, similar to sake
parole.testo: Borrowed from Korean 소주 (soju).

parole.significato: taekwondo
parole.testo: Borrowed from Korean 태권도 (taegwondo).

parole.significato: hangul (Korean phonetic spelling)
parole.testo: Borrowed from Korean 한글 (han'geul), from Archaic Korean ᄒᆞᆫ (“great”) + 글 (geul, “script”).

parole.significato: hanja (Han character script used to write Korean)
parole.testo: Borrowed from Korean 한자(漢字) (hanja), from Middle Chinese 漢字 (MC xanH dziH, “Chinese character”, literally “Han Chinese + character”).

parole.significato: hyung (elder brother, or an affectionate term of address for a somewhat older man)
parole.testo: Borrowed from Korean 형(兄) (hyeong, “older brother of a man”).

parole.significato: jamo (jamo - Korean letters, building blocks of hangeul)
parole.testo: Borrowed from Korean 자모 (jamo) (字母).

parole.significato: chaebol (a large, family-controlled, South Korean business conglomerate)
parole.testo: Borrowed from Korean 재벌(財閥) (jaebeol). Doublet of дзайба́цу (dzajbácu).

parole.significato: kimchi (in a style enjoyed by Soviet Koreans)
parole.testo: Borrowed from Korean 짐치 (jimchi). Essentially from the Soviet Korean dialect (a variety of the Hamgyeong-do dialect).

parole.significato: Juche (the state ideology of North Korea)
parole.testo: Borrowed from Korean 주체 (juche).

parole.significato: yukhoe (a Korean dish)
parole.testo: Borrowed from Korean 육회 (yukhoe).
